newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-AJAX WIN AWAY AT LAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX WIN AWAY AT LAST.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam achieved their first away league victory of the season on Sunday.
They hit Vitesse Arnhem with four second-half goals after trailing early on.
Sixth-placed Vitesse were ahead after three minutes through Dejan Curovic, who beat Netherlands goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar with a free-kick from 20 metres.
They then dominated the rest of the half against an Ajax team missing wingers Tijani Babangida and Marc Overmars and defender Winston Bogarde because of injury.
But Ajax coach Louis van Gaal reshuffled his side during the interval, bringing on Mario Melchiot and Dave van den Bergh.

The changes worked almost immediately. After 48 minutes striker Patrick Kluivert, recently returned from injury, equalised from a rebound after Nordin Wooter's shot was parried by Vitesse goalkeeper Sander Westerveld.

Richard Witschge gave the Dutch champions a 2-1 lead from a free-kick in the 61st minute and in the final half-hour Vitesse's resistance collapsed. Wooter added Ajax's third and van den Bergh the fourth in injury time.
"It was a fantastic victory, considering that last year we lost here even though we were pretty superior," van Gaal said.
Ajax, who play Glagow Rangers in the European Champions' League on Wednesday, moved from sixth to fourth in the table, seven points behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who thrashed Roda JC 8-0 on Saturday.
